nodes.description: The initiating lesion. Homozygous or compound heterozygous DMP1 variants abolish dentin matrix protein 1, a secreted SIBLING-family acidic phosphoprotein expressed by osteocytes, mature osteoblasts and odontoblasts. Reported alleles include start-codon substitutions (p.Met1Val, p.Met1Leu), nonsense variants (p.Trp33Ter, p.Glu32Ter, p.Glu186Ter), frameshifts (p.Glu163ArgfsTer53), splice-site changes (IVS5-1G>A, c.184-1G>A), a 7-bp C-terminal deletion that replaces the last 18 residues with 33 non-native ones, and a 49-kb deletion removing most of the gene. In cells the start-codon mutant never enters the secretory pathway, whereas the C-terminal deletion mutant is secreted but abnormally processed. DMP1 is cleaved in the matrix into a 37-kDa N-terminal and a 57-kDa C-terminal fragment, and the C-terminal fragment alone rescues the null mouse, which matches the observation that patients with C-terminal-affecting alleles are shorter and more hypophosphatemic.

nodes.description: The reference model, from which the human disease was recognized: the hypomineralized bone of the null mouse was known before DMP1 patients were found, and the discovery paper characterized both together. nodes.description: The kidney is structurally normal but hormonally instructed: FGF23 downregulates sodium-phosphate cotransport in the proximal tubule, so phosphate is excreted despite hypophosphatemia. Phosphate wasting is isolated, with normal calcium, normocalciuria and normal parathyroid hormone, which separates the phosphopenic arm from calciopenic rickets and from Fanconi syndrome.

nodes.description: The shared clinical output of the module: soft, undermineralized bone presenting as rickets with open growth plates and osteomalacia after they close, with bone pain, deformity of the weight-bearing long bones, pseudofractures and short stature. ARHR1 adds its own disorder-specific features on top, which are curated as phenotypes: enthesopathy with paraspinal ligament calcification, cranial hyperostosis, a paradoxically high axial bone density, dental disease and hearing impairment.

nodes.description: Osteoid is produced but hydroxyapatite is not deposited into it. In ARHR1 two routes converge here: the substrate deficit of chronic hypophosphatemia, compounded by blunted calcitriol, and the DMP1-intrinsic matrix defect. The convergence is demonstrated by experiment, since restoring phosphate in the null mouse corrects only part of the bone phenotype. The age-dependent expressions are rickets in the growing skeleton and osteomalacia, with pseudofractures and bone pain, in the mature one.

nodes.description: Hypophosphatemia should stimulate 1-alpha-hydroxylation of 25-hydroxyvitamin D; under FGF23 excess it does not, and 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D is inappropriately normal or low. The failed compensation limits intestinal phosphate and calcium absorption and is one reason active vitamin D is part of conventional treatment.
